title: Applied ML: End-to-end Eval Harness, Prompt Sets, Quantization & Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Kapoor
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines an end-to-end process for onboarding models into Redwood’s inference platform, validating them with the eval harness, maintaining prompt sets and benchmarks, producing quantization profiles, and operating a regression triage flow. It consolidates standards and runbooks used by Applied ML, ML Infrastructure, SRE, and Product when adding or changing a model that will be served in Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployments.

Scope:
- New model onboarding (open-source and vendor models)
- Daily/continuous evals and scheduled benchmark runs
- Prompt-set lifecycle and canonical benchmark catalog
- Quantization profile generation and acceptance criteria
- Regression detection, triage, and remediation playbook

Principles:
- Reproducibility: every eval and quantization run must be reproducible from the model hash, config, and prompt-set revision.
- Guardrails first: gated quality checks prevent rollout until minimal metrics are met.
- Observable rollouts: all canary and gradual rollouts must publish telemetry (latency/cost/quality) to the console dashboards.
- Fast detection + prioritized response: regressions must be triaged within 24 hours with clear ownership.

Key components and responsibilities:
- Eval Harness (service: eval-harness-service) \u2014 Maintained by Applied ML. Runs unit-level and scenario-based tests (functional, safety, hallucination, correctness) and stores results in eval-store (time-series + artifact storage).
- Prompt Catalog (service: prompt-catalog) \u2014 Managed by Applied ML + Product. Canonical prompt sets, metadata, and tagging (intent, domain, difficulty, SLO).
- Quantization Registry (service: quant-profile-registry) \u2014 Maintained by ML Infra. Stores quant profiles (per model variant and HW class) and records expected metric deltas.
- Regression Triage Board (board: regression-triage-board) \u2014 Cross-functional: Applied ML owner, SRE on-call, ML Infra, Product PM. Tracks incidents, impact, and remediation.

SLOs and gating thresholds (default):
- Primary quality metric (task-dependent) must not degrade more than 2.0 percentage points vs baseline on full eval suite.
- Safety fales (e.g., toxicity, PII leakage) must be 0 new failures for onboarding; regression tolerance = 0 for safety-critical checks.
- Regression detection window: automated alerts for >3% relative drop on key metric within 24 hours of deployment or new eval run.
- Quantization acceptance: model metric drop <= 1.5 percentage points on primary metric OR within agreed product tolerance.
- Performance: P95 latency for 512-token generation <= 300ms for Hosted-target models; Dedicated targets may be higher depending on config documented in roadmap.

Onboarding checklist (numbered):
1) Model registration:
   - Create model entry in model-catalog with model_hash, architecture, tokenizer_version, source_url, license, and expected FLOPs.
   - Assign preliminary owner (Applied ML) and target serving variants (fp16, int8, quantized-4bit).
2) Baseline evaluation (eval-harness):
   - Run canonical benchmark suite (regression + domain-specific prompt sets) at baseline precision (fp16).
   - Record baseline metrics in eval-store and attach artifacts (predictions, log-prob traces).
3) Prompt-set creation: 
   - Curate prompt sets for: core functionality, edge cases, safety, and adversarial cases. Add metadata: intent, difficulty, expected_output_format.
4) Quantization profiling:
   - Run quantization-pipeline for every target profile in quant-profile-registry (e.g., dyn-8, awq-4, smoothquant-4).
   - Compare metrics vs baseline; annotate profiles with expected metric delta and 95% CI.
5) Guardrail checks & sign-off:
   - Gate 1: Functional and safety checks pass (no new safety failures).
   - Gate 2: Quality delta within tolerance.
   - Stakeholder sign-off: Applied ML lead + Product PM + ML Infra.
6) Canary rollout and monitoring:
   - Canary traffic schedule: 5% (24h) -> 25% (48h) -> 100% (if no regressions). Monitor automated alerts and console dashboards during rollout.
7) Post-rollout evaluation:
   - Run full eval suite on production traffic samples (prefix/KV cache preserved) within 72h and compare to baseline.

Runbook: routine eval-harness execution (daily and on-demand)
1. Triggering:
   - Scheduled: cron job at 03:00 UTC daily for quick checks (reduced prompt sets). Weekly full-suite run on Sundays 02:00 UTC.
   - On-demand: model owner can trigger runs via CLI: evalctl run --model <model_id> --suite full --tag release-2026-09
2. Resources:
   - Quick checks use small CPU/GPU EC2 fleet; full-suite uses eval-cluster G4/G5.
3. Outputs and artifacts:
   - Results are written to eval-store under /models/<model_id>/runs/<run_id>. Artifacts include: metrics.json, predictions.tar.gz, trace.log.
4. Failure modes:
   - If evaluation job fails: auto-retry up to 2 times; on persistent failure alert Applied ML SRE channel and create incident with tag eval-failure.

Regression triage playbook (operational):
1) Detection:
   - Alert triggers from eval-harness or production-monitoring (console alert rule: quality_drop_rule). Threshold = 3% relative drop or safety failure.
2) Triage (first 60 minutes):
   - Pager notifies regression-triage-board. Owner acknowledges and records initial impact: affected model variant, traffic fraction, metric deltas.
3) Root-cause checklist (30-180 minutes):
   - Verify model binary/hash and compare to deployed artifact.
   - Check prompt-set changes and recent changes in prompt-catalog revisions.
   - Inspect quantization profiles and recent quant-profile updates.
   - Check runtime infra (kernel changes, new CUDA/cuDNN versions, driver updates).
   - Re-run failing evals locally on known-good baseline machines.
4) Mitigation options (choose by severity):
   - Immediate rollback to previous model variant (recommended for severe regressions).
   - Switch to unquantized/previous quant profile for affected hardware class.
   - Apply prompt-filtering or prompt-rewrite mitigation for targeted intents.
   - Hotfix model via small prompt-engineered wrapper if acceptable.
5) Postmortem and Preventive actions:
   - Document incident on the incident board within 48 hours with tags: regression, model_id, root_cause.
   - Add new unit tests to eval harness or augment prompt sets to cover the regression case.

Example eval-harness config (JSON, illustrative):
{
  "model_id": "rw-llm-13b-v2",
  "suite": "full",
  "precision": "fp16",
  "prompts": ["core-general", "safety-critical", "domain-finance"],
  "timeout_minutes": "240",
  "artifact_bucket": "s3://eval-store/runs/"
}

Prompt set and benchmark catalog (table view):
| Prompt Set ID | Intent | Size | Owner | Key Metrics |
|---------------|--------|------|-------|-------------|
| core-general  | general QA | 2k | Applied ML | accuracy, exact_match |
| safety-critical | safety | 500 | Safety Team | toxicity_rate, pii_leak_rate |
| domain-finance | finance assistants | 1k | Product (Fin) | correctness, hallucination_rate |

Quantization profile example (table view):
| Profile ID | Algorithm | Target HW | Expected Delta | Owner |
|------------|-----------|-----------|----------------|-------|
| awq-4-amp   | AWQ-4     | A100      | -0.8%          | ML Infra |
| dyn8-eval   | Dynamic8  | T4        | -1.1%          | ML Infra |

Checklist for recording reproducibility metadata (always required):
- model_hash (git + artifact sha256)
- tokenizer_version and vocab sha256
- eval-harness commit SHA and docker image tag
- prompt-set revision id and annotations
- quant-profile id (if used)
- hardware class used for the run

Escalation paths and ownership:
- Applied ML (primary owner) \u2014 onboarding, eval quality, prompt set curation.
- ML Infra \u2014 quantization, build artifacts, runtime kernels.
- SRE \u2014 production monitoring, rollout policies, incident response.
- Product PM \u2014 business metric acceptance and final sign-off.

Appendix: quick commands and examples
- Run a quick eval: evalctl run --model rw-llm-13b-v2 --suite quick --out /tmp/run123
- Trigger a quantization profile: quantctl profile --model rw-llm-13b-v2 --alg awq --bits 4 --out /tmp/awq-profile.json
- Promote profile: quantctl promote --profile /tmp/awq-profile.json --target a100 --tag release-2026-09
